newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX nearby electricity ends up, deferreds mixed.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX nearby electricity ends up, deferreds mixed.

text.p: NYMEX nearby electricity futures settled higher Thursday in a light, choppy session, while deferred contracts finished mixed.
The electricity complex rose in early activity on upward momentum from its recent rise this week.

News that Western Systems Coordinating Council's board approved a capacity increase this spring on the Pacific Intertie to 6,250 megawatt (MW) from 5,200 MW sent the complex lower, brokers and traders said.
This is another step which would increase transport of more cheap hydropower from the Northwest to California and the Southwest.
However, the nearby months managed to rebound in late trading amid steady cash market prices in the western U.S.
Firm, peak electricity for day-ahead delivery at the California-Oregon Border (COB) finished the day at $17.00-18.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) and at Palo Verde (PV) $18.00-22.00.
Spot western power prices were supported by cool weather in the Northwest, air-conditioning demand in the Southwest and ongoing plant outages scattered throughout the West.

At least 4,000 megawatts of generating capacity in the West was off line for maintenance or repairs, although a third of that capacity, primarily coal-fired, was expected to be restored by the weekend.
A 750 MW unit at the coal-fired Four Corners generating complex is expected to resume operation later today.

"It was just very thin with people at the WSPP (Western Systems Power Pool) meeting," said an East Coast paper broker, referring to the group's semi-annual gathering which will take place in Los Angeles Friday.
April COB settled up 19 cents at 11.87/MWh after bouncing between $11.30 and $12.10. May COB ended up 1 cent at $10.85. Other COB months finished mixed.
April PV settled up 1 cent at $15.77 after trading between $15.40 and $16.20. May PV ended five cents higher at $15.20. Other active PV contracts finished flat to 15 cents lower.

Forecasts called for the Pacific Northwest to continue to experience mild, wet weather into the weekend. Readings were expected to run two to four Fahrenheit degrees above average along the coast and four to eight degrees above average in the interior.
In the Southwest, a high pressure system was predicted to push temperatures to eight to 16 degrees above normal through Monday.
